audited_suspected_testing_frame: 98 students admitted as typhoid cases during a known outbreak; active case-finding across 3,313 students
specimen_scope: BLOOD culture only (n=92), stated verbatim; Widal serology on all 98. No stool, urine or bone marrow
case_definition_summary: No standalone syndromic definition. Confirmed = fever >=3 days + positive blood culture; probable = fever >=3 days + positive serodiagnosis without isolation; possible = admitted on clinical suspicion during the outbreak. The effective frame is admission during a known outbreak
testing_selection_mechanism: NEAR-UNIVERSAL, NOT severity-gated. All 98 were admitted to the same military hospital; all 98 had Widal; 'Ninety two blood cultures were taken' (93.9%). The paper does not say why 6 were not cultured. No severity, consent or capacity gate described
temporal_alignment: No epidemic curve printed, though the text references a time-distribution graph showing multiple peaks
denominator_compatibility: COMPATIBLE and the best available: a stated blood-only tested count over a syndromic frame, with 93.9% coverage
simple_model_status: eligible: 5/92 with a stated blood-only denominator and 93.9% coverage
verification_model_status: candidate: lowest verification-bias risk of ANY outbreak study located in this project
audit_notes: THE FIND. 93.9% of suspected cases blood-cultured - better coverage than all three current anchors (Aye 44.9%, Neil 9.4%, Kabwama 3.6%). Positivity 5/92 = 5.4% implies pi ~0.09 at Se_BC 0.62, FAR below Aye 0.26 / Neil 0.58 / Kabwama 0.25. TWO COMPETING EXPLANATIONS THE MODEL CANNOT SEPARATE: (a) genuinely low pi because the denominator is loose - 86/98 were 'probable' on Widal alone at 1/160 H, 1/200 O, so the frame is closer to 'febrile children admitted during an outbreak' than a typhoid syndrome; (b) antibiotic-depressed Se_BC - the authors attribute the low yield to prior antibiotic therapy. Also: the paper reports the same 5 cases as 5.43% (of 92) in the text and 5.10% (of 98) in Table 1.

location: Ercek Village, Van, Eastern Anatolia, Turkey
audited_suspected_testing_frame: 867 suspected village residents, but culture appears confined to the 154 (17.8%) hospitalised
specimen_scope: blood culture (Bactec 9050) AND stool culture, reported separately; Widal on all 154 inpatients
case_definition_summary: Stepladder fever, headache, malaise with loss of appetite, usually with gastrointestinal symptoms, plus >=2 of: toxic look, relative bradycardia, rose spots on trunk, splenic enlargement, non-productive cough
testing_selection_mechanism: SEVERITY-GATED (inferred, never stated). '154 (17.8%) were hospitalized by the treating physician' with no criteria given. All lab work is framed around the 154 inpatients; no lab data of any kind are reported for the 713 non-hospitalised. The paper never states how many of the 154 actually had blood drawn
denominator_compatibility: Blood numerator (34) is recoverable, but the denominator of 154 is INFERRED from percentage arithmetic, not reported. Frame is hospitalised suspects, not all 867
source_status: primary paper reviewed (Zotero JF9DVMSN); Trop Doct 2010;40:160-162
simple_model_status: marginal: usable only as a HOSPITALISED PPV (34/154 = 22.1%)
audit_notes: RESOLVED the abstract's '42 (27.3%) cultures': it is POOLED blood+stool. Text says '34 (22%) cases were confirmed by blood culture and eight (5.2%) by stool culture'; 34/154=22.1%, 8/154=5.2%, 42/154=27.3% - all resolve against 154, confirming the denominator. DO NOT use 42 as a blood numerator. Population 4,700; implied attack rate 18.4%; no deaths. Paper has several internal contradictions (Table 1 ALT >2xULN 12 < ALT >5xULN 13, impossible; ciprofloxacin n=17 in text vs n=15 in Table 2).

audited_suspected_testing_frame: 8 tour participants with fever >38 C for >3 days, defined independently of culture
specimen_scope: BLOOD culture only; stool mentioned only post-treatment for carriage
case_definition_summary: Confirmed = fever >38 C for >3 days AND a positive blood culture for S. Typhi; probable = fever >38 C for >3 days WITHOUT isolation of S. Typhi
testing_selection_mechanism: Not reported. All 8 were admitted across 5 Tokyo hospitals. The 'probable' definition ('without isolation') implies culture was attempted and failed, but this is never stated
temporal_alignment: No figure, but the table is a full line list with individual onset dates
denominator_compatibility: Syndromic frame is defined independently of culture - rare and valuable - but blood_tested=8 is INFERRED from the probable-case wording, not reported
source_status: primary paper reviewed (Zotero B5JQCPES); Emerg Infect Dis 2007;13:1954-1955
simple_model_status: not eligible under the n>=20 rule (n=8)
verification_model_status: candidate on structure, fails on size
audit_notes: 6/8 = 75%. Returning-traveler cohort of 13 (attack rate 62%), non-endemic host population, point-source - a different estimand from endemic community surveillance. Structurally clean but tiny.

specimen_scope: stool AND/OR blood, pooled and unsplittable from the abstract
denominator_compatibility: The 15 confirmed are explicitly 'by stool or blood culture' and cannot be split. In a foodborne outbreak where all typhoid patients had preceding gastroenteritis, stool likely contributed substantially, so 15 is an upper bound on blood-positives
source_status: STILL MISFILED after correction: BOTH Zotero copies (JEMF2WZ7 and AW7IPIVI) contain Borgdorff et al. 2001 on M. tuberculosis. ROOT CAUSE IS PUBLISHER-SIDE: both PDFs carry the stamp academic.oup.com/aje/article/152/10/934/55560. Valenciano is AJE 152(10):934-9; Borgdorff is AJE 154(10):934-43 - same journal, same issue number, same start page, different VOLUME. OUP's URL for the Valenciano article serves the Borgdorff PDF. Re-downloading from that link will fail again
recommended_use: full text retrieval required - by DOI or print/scan, NOT via the OUP link
audit_notes: PMID 11092435; AJE 2000;152(10):934-939. Abstract only: 133 guests with gastroenteritis (attack rate 90%), 27 with typhoid (18%), 15 confirmed by stool OR blood. ~150 guests inferred. Two independent downloads (UQ Library 2015; IVI 2024) are identically wrong, which is the signature of a publisher-side error rather than a local filing mistake.

audited_suspected_testing_frame: None - a designed case-control sample, not a consecutive series
specimen_scope: blood culture (reference standard); RDTs on stored serum
case_definition_summary: No syndromic definition. Cases were blood-culture-confirmed typhoid; controls were febrile patients in four pre-specified diagnostic groups
testing_selection_mechanism: Retrospective selection of archived sera by KNOWN diagnosis. The authors concede: 'the design with previously collected cases and controls, rather than consecutive patients presenting with fever'
denominator_compatibility: pi = 1 by construction. The apparent 49/125 = 39.2% positivity is an artifact of the fixed 49:76 case:control design and must NOT be used
source_status: primary paper reviewed (Zotero GZKSXPCW); Am J Trop Med Hyg 2021;106:543-549
simple_model_status: not eligible: culture-defined cases in a design-fixed ratio
recommended_use: exclude, but retain for two secondary numbers
audit_notes: SECONDARY VALUE despite being ineligible. (1) RDT accuracy vs blood culture: TUBEX Se 77.6/Sp 60.5; Typhidot Rapid 75.5/85.5; Test-It 57.1/93.4 - directly relevant to any future serology-informed PPV layer. (2) Cites background blood-culture positivity in Fiji health facilities = 20% (MHMS 2016 CWMH Pathology report), a facility-level positivity that could inform an endemic-surveillance prior.

audited_suspected_testing_frame: 101/407 nursing-school residents met the clinical case definition for probable typhoid - a clean syndromic frame - but the 9 confirmed cases come from a DIFFERENT, wider population
specimen_scope: acute phase: blood culture (count of tested NOT reported); follow-up: stool culture + PCR + serology only
case_definition_summary: Acute definition not printed; the paper says residents 'met the clinical case definition for probable typhoid fever' without stating it. Follow-up used WHO suspected typhoid (self-reported fever >=3 days)
testing_selection_mechanism: Acute: not reported. Follow-up stool sampling was deliberately non-random - participants in the top and bottom 10% of anti-Vi IgG were approached
denominator_compatibility: DENOMINATOR MISMATCH: the 9 blood-culture-confirmed cases were hospital presenters traced across a primary school, a secondary school AND the nursing school - they are not a subset of the 101. 9/101 would be an invalid PPV
source_status: primary paper reviewed (Zotero XCZ6SHKN); BMC Infect Dis 2023;23:416
simple_model_status: not eligible: numerator and denominator are from different populations
recommended_use: exclude, but retain for the antibiotic finding
audit_notes: CARRIES THE MOST IMPORTANT SIDE-FINDING IN THIS AUDIT: 140/156 (90%) of suspected-typhoid participants had received antibiotics versus 16/212 (7.5%) of non-cases - a 12-fold difference. This quantifies S9 limitation 4 (prior antimicrobial use depresses Se_BC in outbreak settings) with real data. Follow-up recovered ZERO S. Typhi from 49 stool cultures.
